report.summary: The only failure is test_invalid_book_is_rejected[blank-title], where a whitespace-only title ('   ') is accepted and returns 201 instead of 422. The cause is in the app: validate_book checks `if not book.title` (app/main.py:75), which never rejects spaces, while the author check correctly uses `.strip()` (line 77). Fix validate_book to strip the title before the blank check; the other three parametrized cases already pass.

causes.title: Whitespace-only book title is accepted by the API
causes.explanation: validate_book only rejects an empty title, because `not book.title` is False for "   ". The author check on the next line calls `.strip()`, so the title and author rules are inconsistent. The request therefore reaches insert_book and is stored, and the API returns 201. The test is correct to expect 422 for a blank title, and the failure happens on every run, so this is a product bug, not flakiness.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:66: AssertionError: assert 201 == 422 (response 201 Created for book={'title': '   ', 'author': 'A'})
app/main.py:75: `if not book.title:` does not treat "   " as blank
app/main.py:77: `if not book.author.strip():` shows the intended blank-check pattern, which the title check does not follow
app/main.py:153-160: insert_book calls validate_book and then inserts the untrimmed title, so the whitespace title is persisted
causes.suggested_fix: In validate_book (app/main.py:75), change the check to `if not book.title.strip():`. Consider also trimming the title before insert so stored values have no surrounding whitespace. Then rerun tests/api/test_books_api.py to confirm the blank-title case returns 422 with 'Title must not be blank'.
